questions.question: What are pointers in Go, and how do they work?
questions.title: pointers in Go: meaning and behaviour
questions.direct_answer: A pointer stores the address of another value. `&value` obtains an address and `*pointer` reads or changes the value at that address; a pointer's zero value is `nil`. Pointers let a function or method modify shared state and can avoid copying a large value. Go does not support pointer arithmetic, and taking an address is memory-safe because escape analysis keeps the value alive when required.
